questions.question: Why does the indexing stage overlap neighboring chunks by 64 tokens when cutting at ~512 tokens?
options: To increase the number of chunks and dilute retrieval noise
So a sentence straddling a boundary survives intact in both neighboring chunks instead of being cut in half
To let the embedding model process more text per call
To raise the vector store's write throughput
questions.explanation: See the "The indexing stage: compressing documents into a geometric space" section: the overlap guarantees that a sentence straddling a boundary survives intact in both neighboring chunks instead of being cut in half.

questions.question: When assembling the augmented prompt, why does RAG typically lower the temperature (say, 0.2)?
options: A low temperature speeds up vector retrieval
A low temperature curbs the model's unsourced improvisation beyond the material
A low temperature enlarges the usable context window
A low temperature raises the embedding vector dimensions
questions.explanation: See the "The query stage: four steps of one open-book request" section: temperature is usually lowered (say, 0.2) to curb unsourced improvisation.

questions.question: When retrieval misses entirely (the query is semantically unrelated to the store), what does the lesson prescribe?
options: Stuff the top-1 chunk in anyway and let the model answer
Write "if the material is insufficient, say so" into the system prompt, and treat "not found" as a passing answer
Automatically trigger a full re-embedding of the store
Fall back to closed-book mode and let the model complete it from memory
questions.explanation: See the "Traceability, and what open-book cannot fix" section: the one line of defense is to write "if the material is insufficient, say it cannot be found" into the system prompt and treat a "not found" as a passing answer rather than a failure.
